content: I'll start by reading the test image to identify the affected plant part and key visual features.
The test image shows banana fruits (pods) with dark brown/black necrotic rot at the distal tips. This is a classic "tip rot" pattern. Let me check the part index to narrow candidates.

The pod candidates are **Anthracnose** and **Cigar_End_Rot**. The dark necrotic tip rot strongly suggests Cigar End Rot. I'll use my 4 views: one from each of 4 different classes. Starting with Cigar_End_Rot pod reference.
This Cigar End Rot reference shows dark necrotic tips on banana pods - very similar to the test image. Now viewing Anthracnose pod reference.
Anthracnose shows scattered dark spots over the fruit surface - very different from the test image's concentrated tip rot. Now viewing Bunchy_Top reference (class 3 of 4).
Bunchy Top affects leaves with streaks/dots - completely different from the test image. Final reference: Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka (class 4 of 4).

Yellow and Black Sigatoka shows leaf lesions with yellow halos - completely unrelated to the pod tip rot in the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**
- **Test image**: Green banana pods with dark brown/black necrotic rot concentrated at the distal (flower) tips — the "cigar end" pattern
- **Cigar_End_Rot reference**: Perfect match — same dark tip necrosis on green banana fingers
- **Anthracnose reference**: Scattered surface spots across the whole fruit — not tip-concentrated, clearly different
- **Bunchy_Top / Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka**: Leaf diseases entirely — not relevant to pod symptoms

The tip-confined necrotic rot is the pathognomonic sign of Cigar End Rot (*Trachysphaera fructigena*), which attacks the floral remnants and progresses inward from the distal end.
